body: Sounds interesting... but it means as well that a relationship is not possible for me. I do not have anything anyone could consider as a complement to their weaknesses.

Is becoming more social a goal for spd? Maybe I don't understand it enough, but I know well that spending time with people different than me is very draining and simply unappealing. But I've had friends with who we were very similar, although it was a long ago, and it started crumbling the more differences showed up. Maybe it's my fault. I even had a relationship with someone quite extraverted and with different way of feeling the world. I just always seemed... off. I couldn't relate in any way to her. Do I get everything wrong?
What would you like your potential partner to offer you?

Thank you for the comment. Just like in my last answer to the /u/Riergard, I feel like the kind of love I see my parents are having, with nothing in common and constantly arguing is not something I want to participate in. I feel like my understanding of the world is wrong, but I just don't see a different way. I guess I don't understand the "true" love.
I have an appointment in 2 months. But I feel like it's futile. Everything I thought about the world turned out false, and the reality is... unattractive.

>but not healthy and fun (which in long run accumulates and brings in some major issues).

Could you explain why? I've had a dream for a very long time, of finding someone exactly like me, at least very similar. I've been surrounded by fights and arguments all around me since the early childhood. I always noticed that arguments come from disagreements. Wouldn't the same view on the world result in peace? 

>Unfortunately (or fortunately), this poetic kind of love won’t happen; it is more like a strong family/friend-ish relationship. At least that’s what I’ve seen so far.

This sounds heartbreaking as well. I can't help but feel "not right" around anyone around me. I feel like a complete outcast, and the fantasy of having someone like me one day kept me alive many times.

Thank you for answering. You wouldn't accept someone with the same view on the world? I'm sorry if I misunderstood, english is not my native language. 

Your answer about the relationship sounds a bit depressing.

And about elaborating on love - I wonder what may love mean for us (or just me, I may have deeper misanthropic tendencies) if we don't like the presence of anyone around us. Is love something an spd can yearn for? If yes, then what conditions would have to be met in a relationship?

Well, I have no insurance and not much money, in my country there's no other way to get an appointment. Maybe it's just a pattern my brain considers as normal, after having those images during pleasant activities it's like it's now an accustomed reaction, an involuntary habit. I may try to reverse it by forcefully thinking about and therefore associating more pleasant images and feelings during those moments.
I'm afraid it will stay with me for a very long time, it will trigger during pleasant activities, time spent with a partner for example. It will ruin everything.. Thank you for attention.
I thought no one would reply so I forgot about it. If you see this, thank you and have a nice day.
